mcqs.stem: Best guess: a client's income will be much higher next year because of a large bonus. Generally, what should she do with deductible expenses she controls?

choices.text: Pay them this year, as early as possible
choices.explanation: Deductions are worth more in the higher-rate year.

choices.text: It makes no difference when they're paid
choices.explanation: The marginal rate differs between years.

choices.text: Delay them to next year's higher rate
choices.explanation: Correct. A deduction saves tax at the marginal rate, so it is worth more in the higher-rate year.

mcqs.explanation: A deduction saves tax at the marginal rate, so it is worth more in the higher-rate year.

mcqs.stem: Prior-year AGI was $120,000 and prior-year tax was $18,000. Current-year tax will be $30,000. What is the required annual payment to avoid a penalty?

choices.explanation: 90% of current-year tax is larger than the prior-year safe harbor.
The safe harbors allow less than 100% of current tax.
110% applies only when prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000.

mcqs.explanation: AGI of $120,000 uses the 100% prior-year safe harbor: lesser of $27,000 or $18,000.

mcqs.stem: Bunching itemized deductions produces the most benefit when a taxpayer's annual itemized deductions are:

choices.explanation: Correct. Bunching lets the taxpayer itemize in one year and take the standard deduction in the other.

choices.text: Far above the standard deduction every year
choices.explanation: They already itemize every year; bunching adds little.

choices.text: Made up only of state income taxes
choices.explanation: SALT timing is limited by the cap and payment rules.

mcqs.explanation: Bunching lets the taxpayer itemize in one year and take the standard deduction in the other.

mcqs.stem: Kim's 2024 AGI was $180,000 and her 2024 tax was $30,000. Her 2025 tax will be $50,000. What required annual payment avoids the underpayment penalty for 2025?

choices.explanation: The prior-year safe harbor is lower.

mcqs.explanation: High-income taxpayers use 110% of prior-year tax.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer owes $900 when filing after withholding. What underpayment penalty applies?

choices.text: None; the balance due is under $1,000
choices.explanation: Correct. §6654(e)(1): no penalty if tax due after withholding is less than $1,000.
That's the failure-to-pay rate, which applies only if the balance isn't paid by the due date.

mcqs.explanation: §6654(e)(1): no penalty if tax due after withholding is less than $1,000.

mcqs.stem: A self-employed client earned most of his 2025 income in December. Which method most likely reduces his estimated-tax penalty?

choices.explanation: An extension doesn't extend payment deadlines.

choices.text: Paying the full balance due on January 15
choices.explanation: Earlier installments would still be short under the regular method.
Correct. The annualized method matches required installments to when income was actually earned.

mcqs.explanation: The annualized method matches required installments to when income was actually earned.

mcqs.stem: Single taxpayer: wages $180,000, dividends $30,000, and long-term capital gains $20,000. What is the NIIT?
Which income is **not** net investment income for the 3.8% NIIT?

choices.text: Rent from a passive rental property

choices.explanation: Correct. Qualified retirement plan and IRA distributions are excluded from NII.

mcqs.explanation: Qualified retirement plan and IRA distributions are excluded from NII.

mcqs.stem: A married couple filing jointly has wages of $150,000 (spouse A) and $160,000 (spouse B). How much additional Medicare tax do they owe?

choices.explanation: Combined wages exceed the MFJ threshold.

mcqs.explanation: MFJ threshold is $250,000 of combined wages; neither employer withholds (each is under $200,000), so it's paid with the return.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 15-year-old has $6,000 of interest income and no earned income in 2025. How much of it is taxed at the parents' rate?

choices.explanation: The first $2,700 isn't taxed at the parents' rate.
The kiddie tax applies to children under 19.

mcqs.explanation: 2025 kiddie tax threshold: $2,700 ($1,350 standard deduction + $1,350 at the child's rate).

mcqs.stem: In 2025, a client age 74 must take a $40,000 RMD and plans to give $40,000 to charity. She takes the standard deduction. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Take the RMD in cash and donate it
choices.explanation: Increases AGI; no deduction benefit because she doesn't itemize.

choices.text: Have the IRA pay the charity directly (a QCD)
choices.explanation: Correct. A QCD satisfies the RMD and is excluded from income — better than a deduction she can't use.

choices.text: Skip the RMD and donate from savings
choices.explanation: Missing an RMD triggers an excise tax.

choices.text: Convert the IRA to a Roth IRA first
choices.explanation: Conversion is taxable and doesn't satisfy the RMD.

mcqs.explanation: A QCD satisfies the RMD and is excluded from income — better than a deduction she can't use.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer expects to move from the 24% bracket in 2025 to the 35% bracket in 2026. Which action most likely reduces total tax over the two years?

choices.text: Accelerate a deductible charitable gift into 2025

choices.explanation: Correct. When rates will rise, pull income into the lower-rate year and push deductions into the higher-rate year.
Gain rates may rise with income.
Converting at the lower rate is better.

mcqs.explanation: When rates will rise, pull income into the lower-rate year and push deductions into the higher-rate year.

mcqs.stem: In 2025, a married couple filing jointly with MAGI of $300,000 pays $45,000 of state income and property taxes. What is their SALT itemized deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. MAGI is under $500,000, so the full $40,000 cap applies.

mcqs.explanation: P.L. 119-21 raised the SALT cap to $40,000 for 2025, reduced only when MAGI exceeds $500,000.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date for 2025. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: Which strategy lets a taxpayer claim a large charitable deduction now while recommending grants to charities over several years?

choices.explanation: A QCD isn't a deduction and goes straight to a charity.
Correct. A donor-advised fund contribution is deductible when made; grants can be recommended later.

mcqs.explanation: A donor-advised fund contribution is deductible when made; grants can be recommended later.

mcqs.stem: A client's will leaves everything to her children, but her IRA beneficiary designation still names her former spouse. She dies. Who receives the IRA?

choices.explanation: Correct. Beneficiary designations control retirement accounts and override the will.
The will does not govern assets that pass by beneficiary designation.
A named beneficiary receives the account outside probate.
The designation, not a compromise, controls.

mcqs.explanation: Review beneficiary designations after life events; they pass outside probate and override the will (subject to any state revocation-on-divorce statute).

mcqs.stem: Which risk can an investor reduce by holding a diversified portfolio?

choices.explanation: Interest rate changes affect the whole market; diversification does not remove systematic risk.
Correct. Diversification reduces unsystematic risk; systematic (market) risk remains.
A recession affects nearly all securities.

mcqs.explanation: Diversification reduces unsystematic risk only.

mcqs.stem: A client wants to harvest a loss on an S&P 500 index fund in December but stay invested in the market. Which action achieves both?

choices.text: Buy a fund on another index
choices.explanation: Correct. It isn't substantially identical, so no wash sale.

choices.text: Rebuy the same fund in 2 weeks
Buy the same fund in her IRA
Sell and rebuy it the same day

mcqs.explanation: §1091 disallows a loss if substantially identical securities are bought within 30 days before or after the sale, including in the taxpayer's IRA.

mcqs.stem: A client plans to give $50,000 to her church. She owns stock held 5 years (basis $10,000; FMV $50,000). Which approach is most tax-efficient?

choices.text: Sell the stock and donate the cash
choices.explanation: She'd pay tax on the gain.
Correct. She deducts FMV and avoids the $40,000 gain.

choices.text: Donate cash and keep the stock
Donate it after a year-end sale

mcqs.explanation: Gifts of long-term appreciated stock to a public charity give an FMV deduction (subject to 30% of AGI) and avoid capital gains tax.

mcqs.stem: A client has an unusually low-income year after leaving her job. Which planning step may be worthwhile?

choices.explanation: Correct. Conversion income is taxed at low rates.
The low year is the opportunity.

mcqs.explanation: A low-income year can be used to convert traditional IRA money to a Roth at low marginal rates.

mcqs.stem: A client has room in the 0% capital gains bracket. What can she do with appreciated stock?

choices.text: Hold it to avoid any tax
Gift it to a high earner

mcqs.explanation: Gains realized within the 0% bracket aren't taxed, and the wash sale rule doesn't apply to gains.

mcqs.stem: Why is an HSA sometimes called a triple-tax-advantaged account?

choices.text: It avoids estate and gift tax
Tax benefits in, during and out
choices.explanation: Correct. All three stages are favored.

choices.text: It's exempt from state tax everywhere

mcqs.explanation: HSA contributions are deductible, earnings grow tax-free, and qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free.

mcqs.stem: A parent wants to shift $10,000 of investment income to her 12-year-old. What limits the benefit?

choices.explanation: Correct. Unearned income is taxed at parents' rates.

mcqs.explanation: The kiddie tax taxes a child's unearned income above a threshold at the parents' rates.

mcqs.stem: A client wants to give her grandson stock worth less than her basis. What should she do instead?

choices.explanation: Correct. A gift would waste the loss.
The grandson can't use her loss.

choices.text: Give it to a charity instead

mcqs.explanation: Built-in losses don't transfer to a donee for loss purposes, so selling and gifting cash preserves the deduction.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer owns a rental business that generates $80,000 of net income and pays NIIT on it. Which change could remove that income from NIIT?

choices.text: Collecting more of the rent in cash
choices.explanation: The form of payment doesn't matter.

choices.text: Treating the rental as a hobby

choices.explanation: Correct. Nonpassive trade or business income isn't NII.

mcqs.explanation: Rental income of a real estate professional who materially participates in a trade or business isn't NII.

mcqs.stem: A couple's itemized deductions are $15,000 a year plus $20,000 of annual charitable gifts; the standard deduction is $30,000 each year. If they bunch two years of gifts into Year 1 and take the standard deduction in Year 2, how much do total deductions change over the two years?
mcqs.explanation: Bunching: Year 1 itemize $55,000; Year 2 standard $30,000 = $85,000, versus $70,000 itemizing both years.

mcqs.stem: A grandparent in the 35% bracket holds appreciated stock and wants to fund her 25-year-old grandson's graduate school. The grandson's income is low, and he isn't subject to the kiddie tax. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Sell the stock and give cash
choices.explanation: She'd pay tax at 15% or more.

choices.text: Give the stock; let him sell it
choices.explanation: Correct. His gain may be taxed at 0% with the carryover basis.

choices.text: Lend him the cash at no interest

mcqs.explanation: Gifting appreciated stock shifts the gain to a low-bracket donee who may qualify for the 0% rate.

mcqs.stem: What is the 2025 standard deduction for a married couple filing jointly?
mcqs.explanation: For 2025, the standard deduction is $31,500 for joint filers and $15,750 for single filers.

mcqs.stem: For 2025, above what amount is a child's unearned income taxed at the parents' rate under the kiddie tax?
mcqs.explanation: For 2025, a child's unearned income above $2,700 is taxed at the parents' marginal rate.

mcqs.stem: For a taxpayer with prior-year AGI above $150,000, what prior-year safe harbor avoids the estimated tax penalty?

choices.explanation: That's for AGI of $150,000 or less.

mcqs.explanation: Taxpayers with prior-year AGI over $150,000 must pay 110% of prior-year tax (or 90% of current-year tax) to avoid the penalty.

mcqs.stem: A single 67-year-old has 2025 MAGI of $95,000. What senior deduction may she claim?
mcqs.explanation: The 2025–2028 senior deduction of $6,000 is reduced by 6% of MAGI over $75,000 ($150,000 joint).

mcqs.stem: A single server receives $30,000 of qualified tips in 2025, with MAGI of $90,000. What tips deduction applies?

choices.explanation: Correct. The deduction is capped at $25,000.

mcqs.explanation: Qualified tips are deductible up to $25,000 a year (2025–2028), phasing out above $150,000 of MAGI ($300,000 joint).

mcqs.stem: A single worker earns a $15,000 qualified overtime premium in 2025, with MAGI of $100,000. What overtime deduction applies?
mcqs.explanation: Qualified overtime compensation is deductible up to $12,500 ($25,000 joint) for 2025–2028.

mcqs.stem: A joint filer pays $45,000 of state and local taxes in 2025, and MAGI is $560,000. What is the SALT deduction?
mcqs.explanation: For 2025, the $40,000 SALT cap is reduced by 30% of MAGI over $500,000, but not below $10,000.

mcqs.stem: A joint filer pays $50,000 of state and local taxes in 2025, with MAGI of $700,000. What is the SALT deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. The phase-down stops at the floor.

mcqs.explanation: The SALT cap can't be reduced below $10,000 ($5,000 MFS).

mcqs.stem: A single filer has 2025 AMTI of $200,000. The exemption is $88,100 and isn't phased out. What is tentative minimum tax?
mcqs.explanation: Tentative minimum tax applies 26% (then 28%) to AMTI above the exemption.

mcqs.stem: A 12-year-old has $6,700 of interest and dividends in 2025. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?
mcqs.explanation: Unearned income above the threshold is taxed at the parents' rate.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer pays $12,000 of interest on a loan for a new U.S.-assembled personal car in 2025. MAGI is $80,000. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: Car loan interest is now deductible.

mcqs.explanation: For 2025–2028, interest on loans for new U.S.-assembled personal vehicles is deductible up to $10,000.

mcqs.stem: A joint filer with two qualifying children has 2025 AGI of $420,000. What child tax credit applies?
mcqs.explanation: The $2,200 credit per child is reduced by $50 per $1,000 of AGI over $400,000 (joint).

mcqs.stem: AGI is $100,000, and unreimbursed medical expenses are $12,000. What medical deduction applies?
mcqs.explanation: Medical expenses are deductible above 7.5% of AGI.

mcqs.stem: In 2026, a single non-itemizer gives $1,500 in cash to a public charity. What deduction applies?
mcqs.explanation: Starting in 2026, non-itemizers may deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 joint) of cash gifts to public charities.

mcqs.stem: Prior-year tax was $40,000 (AGI $180,000). Current-year tax is $60,000. What is the minimum required annual estimated payment?

choices.explanation: The prior-year safe harbor is lower.

mcqs.explanation: The required annual payment is the lesser of 90% of current tax or 110% of prior tax for high-AGI filers.

mcqs.stem: Parents support their 23-year-old full-time student, who earned $6,000. May they claim the child as a dependent?

choices.text: No, the child is too old

choices.explanation: The child qualifies as a qualifying child.

choices.text: No, the income is too high

choices.explanation: Correct. Students under 24 meet the age test.

mcqs.explanation: A full-time student under 24 can be a qualifying child; the gross income test applies only to qualifying relatives.

mcqs.stem: A single filer has MAGI of $250,000 and $80,000 of net investment income. What NIIT applies?
mcqs.explanation: NIIT is 3.8% of the lesser of NII or MAGI above $200,000 (single).

mcqs.stem: A joint filer has $25,000 of other itemized deductions and gives $10,000 a year to charity. How much more can she deduct over 2 years by bunching both gifts into one year?
mcqs.explanation: Bunching deductions into alternate years lets taxpayers itemize in one year and take the standard deduction in the other.

mcqs.stem: In which year is a Roth conversion generally most efficient?

choices.text: A year with a large bonus

choices.explanation: Correct. Conversion income is taxed at lower rates.

mcqs.explanation: Converting in low-income years minimizes tax on the converted amount.

mcqs.stem: Parents give appreciated stock to their 15-year-old, who sells it. What is the likely tax result?

choices.text: All gain is taxed at the child's rate
The gain is tax-free to all

mcqs.explanation: Shifting gains to children under 19 (or students under 24) is limited by the kiddie tax.

mcqs.stem: Two single taxpayers, each paying $40,000 of state taxes, plan to marry. What happens to their combined SALT deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. One $40,000 cap applies to a joint return.

mcqs.explanation: The SALT cap is the same for joint and single filers, creating a marriage penalty.

mcqs.stem: A single 70-year-old has MAGI of $95,000. How much would deferring $20,000 of income to next year raise this year's senior deduction?

choices.explanation: Correct. The 6% phase-out would be removed.

mcqs.explanation: Managing MAGI around phase-out thresholds can increase income-based deductions.

mcqs.stem: In November, a taxpayer finds she underpaid estimated tax for the first three quarters. What is the best fix?

choices.text: Wait and pay with the return

choices.explanation: Correct. Withholding is treated as paid evenly.

mcqs.explanation: Withholding is treated as paid ratably during the year, so increasing it late in the year can cure earlier underpayments.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer's 2024 AGI was $140,000 and 2024 tax was $22,000. Her 2025 tax will be $35,000 and withholding will be $15,000. What minimum estimated payments avoid the underpayment penalty?

choices.explanation: Uses 110% of prior-year tax, but AGI didn't exceed $150,000.
Correct. Required payment = lesser of 31,500 or 22,000; 22,000 − 15,000.

mcqs.explanation: 100% of prior-year tax applies because prior AGI was ≤ $150,000.

mcqs.stem: Which item is included in net investment income for the 3.8% NIIT?

choices.text: Wages paid to her by an S corporation
Qualified distributions from a Roth IRA
Gain on the sale of a vacation home
choices.explanation: Correct. Gain on disposition of property not held in an active business is NII.

mcqs.explanation: Gain on disposition of property not held in an active business is NII.

mcqs.stem: A married couple filing jointly has MAGI of $270,000, including $40,000 of net investment income. What is their NIIT?

choices.explanation: Uses NII instead of the smaller MAGI excess.

mcqs.explanation: Base = lesser of 40,000 NII or 20,000 excess → 3.8% × 20,000 = 760.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 17-year-old full-time high school student has $10,000 of dividend income in 2025 and no earned income. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?

choices.explanation: The first $2,700 isn't taxed at the parents' rate.

mcqs.explanation: 2025 kiddie tax threshold: $2,700.

mcqs.stem: Which planning step most likely reduces a client's AGI while satisfying her charitable goal and her 2025 RMD (age 74)?

choices.text: Donate appreciated stock she has held for 5 years
choices.explanation: Deduction, but not an AGI exclusion or an RMD.

choices.text: Donate cash from a taxable brokerage account
Make a qualified charitable distribution from the IRA
choices.explanation: Correct. QCDs are excluded from income and count toward the RMD.

choices.text: Take the RMD and give it to a donor-advised fund

mcqs.explanation: QCDs are excluded from income and count toward the RMD.

mcqs.stem: A single taxpayer with 2025 MAGI of $550,000 pays $50,000 of state and local taxes. What is her SALT deduction?

choices.explanation: The cap is reduced above $500,000 MAGI.
The floor applies only if the reduction goes further.

mcqs.explanation: P.L. 119-21: $40,000 cap reduced by 30% of MAGI over $500,000, not below $10,000.
mcqs.reviewNote: Uses a One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) amount or effective date. Verify against current IRS guidance and exam materials.

mcqs.stem: Which item is a tax preference or adjustment for individual AMT?

choices.explanation: Correct. Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.
Acquisition interest is allowed for AMT.
Allowed at the same floor for AMT.

mcqs.explanation: Private activity bond interest is an AMT preference.

mcqs.stem: A self-employed client will realize a large capital gain in December 2025 and made no estimated payments earlier because her income was low. Which approach can reduce or eliminate an underpayment penalty for the earlier installments?

choices.explanation: Correct. It matches each required installment to income actually earned through that period.

choices.text: Paying the full year's tax on January 15, 2026
choices.explanation: A late payment doesn't cure earlier underpaid installments.

choices.text: Filing a six-month extension for the return
choices.explanation: An extension doesn't extend payment deadlines.

choices.text: Electing to treat the gain as received in 2026
choices.explanation: Timing can't be elected after the sale.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §6654(d)(2): the annualized income installment method lets a taxpayer with uneven income base installments on income earned through each period.

mcqs.stem: Which item is excluded from net investment income for the 3.8% NIIT?

choices.text: Rental income from a passive rental activity

choices.explanation: Correct. Qualified plan and IRA distributions aren't net investment income.

choices.text: Gain on the sale of investment land
choices.explanation: Gains on investment property are NII.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §1411(c)(5): distributions from qualified plans and IRAs are excluded from net investment income; wages and active business income are also excluded.

mcqs.stem: A client expects to move from the 24% bracket in 2025 to the 35% bracket in 2026. Which year-end strategy is most likely to reduce her total tax?

choices.text: Defer income to 2026 and accelerate deductions into 2025
choices.explanation: That reverses the benefit when rates rise.

choices.text: Accelerate both income and deductions into 2025
choices.explanation: Deductions are worth more in the higher-rate year.

choices.text: Accelerate income into 2025 and defer deductions to 2026
choices.explanation: Correct. Income is taxed at the lower 2025 rate, and deductions are worth more at 35%.

choices.text: Defer both income and deductions to 2026
choices.explanation: Income would be taxed at the higher rate.

mcqs.explanation: When the marginal rate will rise, accelerate income and defer deductions; reverse when rates will fall.

mcqs.stem: A client exercises incentive stock options with a $100,000 bargain element and holds the shares. How does the exercise affect her 2025 taxes?

choices.text: $100,000 of ordinary income for regular tax
choices.explanation: ISO exercises don't create regular income.
There is no sale, so no gain.
Correct. The ISO spread is an AMT preference-type adjustment only.

choices.text: No effect on either regular tax or AMT

mcqs.explanation: IRC §56(b)(3): the ISO bargain element is an AMT adjustment in the year of exercise (if the shares are held); AMT paid can create a minimum tax credit.

mcqs.stem: A client who usually takes the standard deduction gives about $6,000 a year to charity. Which strategy most likely increases the tax benefit of her giving in 2025?

choices.text: Spread the gifts evenly over each month of the year
choices.explanation: Timing within the year doesn't change itemizing.

choices.text: Give cash instead of appreciated stock
choices.explanation: Appreciated stock avoids capital gains tax.

choices.text: Make the gifts to a private foundation
choices.explanation: Foundation gifts have lower AGI limits.

choices.text: Bunch gifts into one year via a donor-advised fund
choices.explanation: Correct. Bunching pushes itemized deductions above the standard deduction in one year.

mcqs.explanation: Bunching gifts — often through a donor-advised fund — lets the donor itemize in the bunching year and take the standard deduction in others.

mcqs.stem: For 2025 the kiddie-tax threshold is $2,700. A 15-year-old dependent has $5,000 of interest income and no earned income. How much is taxed at the parents' rate?

choices.explanation: The first $2,700 isn't taxed at the parents' rate.
Unearned income above the threshold is taxed at the parents' rate.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §1(g): a child's net unearned income above the threshold ($2,700 for 2025) is taxed at the parents' rate.

flashcards.back: Lesser of 90% of current-year tax or 100% of prior-year tax (110% if prior AGI > $150,000). No penalty under $1,000 due.
3.8% × lesser of NII or MAGI over $200,000 single / $250,000 MFJ.
0.9% on wages/SE income over $200,000 single / $250,000 MFJ; employer withholds above $200,000.

Unearned income above the threshold of a child under 19 (under 24 if a full-time student with earned income not over half of support) is taxed at the parents' rate. (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
Concentrate itemized deductions (e.g., donor-advised fund) in alternating years.
Direct IRA-to-charity transfer at age 70½ or older: excluded from income, counts toward the RMD, no charitable deduction. (The exam gives the dollar amount.)
